title: I’m going to need a sequel with Mama Rose as a lesbian murderess #gyp...
transcript: Y'all, the real Mama Rose had a body count, and we need to talk about it. I recently went to see a production of what I consider to be one of the greatest musicals ever written that is, unfortunately, titled Gypsy. Uh, you know, other than that, though, it is perfect. And if you're not familiar with the musical, it is based off of the real childhood of burlesque star Gypsy Rose Lee, her sister June, and, of course, her mother, rose. And anytime I see a show that is based on historical events, I like to go down a rabbit hole to see, like, what is actually accurate. And, y'all, the most wild things in the story did not make the musical. So here are some of my favorite facts about the real life Rose, June, and Louise. And of course, we have to start off with Mama Rose, who has a body count, committed a lot of crimes in her life, and some of them are depicted in the musical, like stealing silverware or hijacking other people's acts. But she would also steal bed sheets. She would leave hotels without paying them. And at one point, she threw a hotel manager out a window to his death. She ended up getting off, claiming self defense, but, like, like he died, she murdered him. Mama Rose was also possibly bisexual, or at least a late in life lesbian. Near the end of her life, she ran a boarding house. Most of the tenants were lesbians, and she had multiple female partners. One of the women ended up dying in her boarding house of a gunshot wound. The police claimed that it was self inflicted, but later in life, Louise own son did interviews claiming that rose had killed the woman because she was her partner and she had hit on her daughter Louise. And like, given the violence earlier in her life, I wouldn't put it past her, honestly. In the musical, the character of Tulsa is based off of vaudeville performer Bobby Reid that performed with them and did run off and get married with June one. This happened when June was 16, but she thought she was 13 at the time because they did in fact lie about their ages and had multiple birth certificates. After finding out that they had eloped, rose was furious, went to the cops to have Bobby arrested, and the cops were like, uh, we can't do anything. It's just marriage. And so instead she pulls a gun on Bobby and pulls the trigger, but the safety was on, so he was fine. Bobby and June ended up running off. Obviously they got divorced, but they ended up working together 4 years dancing on the Marathon circuit to make ends meet. June started her career off as Baby June because she literally started off as a baby. She was 2 when she started dancing on point and being a parade around as A vaudeville act, and in the 30s both June and Louise ended up performing on Broadway. One of my favorite facts is that Louise ended up in the 1936 Zigfield Follies with Fanny Bryce, when June was a Broadway actress for decades from the 30s to the 80s. Her final role is actually the closing Miss Hannigan in the original production of Annie. Both of them ended up writing memoirs. Louis, of course, wrote Gypsy that ended up getting turned into the musical. She was originally offered $200,000 to turn it into a film, but decided against that and instead handing it over for theatrical rights because she figured she could make more money from that. And ultimately that decision is kind of what cemented all 3 of their legacy for the long term.
